metadata.title: Now you can use vcpkg to get some of the dependencies.

issue_payload.body: This feature can be enabled by defining the `USE_VCPKG` flag when running `cmake ..` (so instead of just `cmake ..`, do `cmake -DUSE_VCPKG=ON ..`). Tested on Windows 10 with Visual Studio 2019 and the latest vcpkg commit.


issue_payload.body:
Version information may now be encapsulated inside an object that can be compared.
Here is a short break down on the changes of the individual commits which may be cherry-picked if only parts are desired:

- 0cd06ae Introduces the Version class
- 67bc173 Adds an instance of a Version object for the current repository state to obe::Config
- f631218 Remove requirement for git to reside in PATH
- 585927f Move configure_file mechanism into separate CMake file ( engine_git.cmake ) since it would only be run on reconfiguration otherwise.

When using "configure_file" the files will only be updated during configure time. If you create a new commit and build your project, the changes will not be reflected in the build unless you reconfigure the CMake project.

metadata.title: Adds AABB filtering for collision check (closes #310)

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Transform/Rect.hpp] Duplicate of intersects method ?

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [src/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.cpp] Maybe put this code inside a private function (not a method) so it doesn't appear twice ?

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [src/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.cpp] Single `doesCollide` doesn't have bounding-box optimization anymore ?

discussion_timeline.author: Darnagof
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Transform/Rect.hpp] It return a boolean if there is an intersection, but doesn't calculate the Rect intersection.

discussion_timeline.author: Darnagof
discussion_timeline.body:
[src/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.cpp] The bounding-box optimization is already made in doesCollide(offset) and getMaximumDistanceBeforeCollision(offset). It avoids the process being made twice during collision detection.
An alternative would be to keep the optimization but add a boolean parameter to skip this process.

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [src/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.cpp] Yup, I would keep the optimization, it's pretty useful when you want custom collision logic (such as climbing ladders etc..)

discussion_timeline.author: Darnagof
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Transform/Rect.hpp] I made this function to avoid doing the Rect calculation of the intersection, because the AABB filter doesn't need it. I tried using doesIntersects() and intersects() on AABB filtering on a same benchmark scenario, and with doesIntersects() we get ~0.30% less Total CPU usage on getMaximumDistanceBeforeCollision().

commit_history.message: private aabbFilter function + renamed intersects to getIntersection
commit_history.author: Darnagof

issue_payload.body:
Added `CollisionData `struct, returned by `collider.getMaximumDistanceBeforeCollision`.
Now a vector of touched colliders is sent to `OnCollide` callback.
Now `collider.doesCollide()` return a vector of touched colliders.

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.hpp] Why not returning a CollisionData here too ?

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body:
[include/Core/Collision/Trajectory.hpp] Might be better to change 
```cpp
UnitVector, std::vector<PolygonalCollider*>&
```
to
```cpp
CollisionData
```

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [src/Core/Bindings/Collision/Collision.cpp] Make it readonly please :)

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [src/Core/Bindings/Collision/Collision.cpp] Also readonly

discussion_timeline.author: Darnagof
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.hpp] Because `doesCollide` only check the colliders that can be touched in the offset, it doesn't return a new calculated offset (contrary to `getMaximumDistanceBeforeCollision`).

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: [include/Core/Collision/PolygonalCollider.hpp] You can always return a zero offset, it makes the API clearer and allows the user to benefit tof future methods of `CollisionData`.

discussion_timeline.author: Sygmei
discussion_timeline.body: Good job ! You can now merge :)
